note: Simplified view of UniFest (github.com/abigailsadom1903/UniFest), a five-person team project. Component names match real files; the admin/, user_dashboard/ and feedback/ folders are separate prototypes and are not shown.

nodes.title: Browser
nodes.summary: Students, staff, public visitors and admins use UniFest through server-rendered pages.
details: A shared header shows the navigation and a bell with the number of unread notifications.
Login and registration pages have their own full-screen design.

nodes.title: Event catalogue
nodes.summary: The home page lists approved events, with search by name and a filter by category.
details: Visitors who are not signed in see only public events; university-only events appear after signing in.
Opening a university-only event while signed out redirects to the login page.

nodes.title: Accounts & roles
nodes.summary: Registration, sign-in and four roles: admin, staff, student and public.
details: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt on registration and checked with password_verify on sign-in.
Suspended accounts cannot sign in.
The user's ID, name and role are kept in the PHP session and checked on every protected page.

nodes.title: Role-based dashboard
nodes.summary: One dashboard that changes with the user's role.
details: Admins see system totals, every event, and links to Manage Users and Reports.
Staff and students see the events they organise; everyone sees the events they joined.

nodes.title: Event management
nodes.summary: Organisers create, edit and delete their events; admins approve or archive them.
details: New events start as 'pending' and appear in the catalogue only after an admin approves them.
Edit and delete check that the user is the event's organiser or an admin.
Posters are uploaded as JPG, PNG or GIF files.

nodes.title: Registrations & participants
nodes.summary: Users join or cancel events; organisers view participants, take attendance and send updates.
details: The event page checks for an existing registration before adding a new one.
Organisers can mark participants present, export the list as CSV, and broadcast a message to everyone registered.

nodes.title: Administration
nodes.summary: Admins manage users and produce event reports.
details: Users can be suspended, reactivated, deleted, or (for staff) promoted to admin.
Reports filter events by month and category.

nodes.title: Data access (PDO)
nodes.summary: Pages query MySQL through one shared PDO connection.
details: Queries that include user input use prepared statements with ? parameters, including search and report filters.
PDO is set to throw exceptions on database errors.

nodes.title: MySQL database
nodes.summary: Five tables for users, events, registrations, feedback and notifications.
details: Event type, mode, status and visibility, and user role and status, are ENUM columns.
Foreign keys decide what happens on delete: events and feedback cascade, registrations block the delete.
Explore every table in the Data model tab.

nodes.title: Notifications & email
nodes.summary: In-app notifications are stored in the database; emails are simulated by writing them to a log file.
details: addNotification saves a message for a user; opening the notifications page marks them as read.
sendEmail writes each email to email_log.txt, so the flow can be demonstrated without a mail server.

nodes.title: Poster storage
nodes.summary: Uploaded posters are saved in assets/uploads with a timestamped file name; the database stores the name.
details: events.poster holds the file name, and event pages fall back to a placeholder when it is empty.

steps.text: A student or staff member fills in the event form and uploads a poster.
The poster is checked for an image type and saved with a timestamped name.
The event is stored with status 'pending'.
The admin sees the pending event with Approve and Reject links.
The organiser gets a notification that the event was approved.
The event now appears in the catalogue.
A signed-in user opens an event and clicks to join.
The page checks the user is not already registered.
A prepared INSERT adds the registration.
The participant and the organiser both get a notification, and a confirmation email is logged.
The user enters their email and password.
The account is looked up by email with a prepared statement.
password_verify checks the password, and suspended accounts are refused.
The session stores the user's role and the dashboard opens.
